utterances.text: So, in the first chart, we have the Rajlovac and Vogosca Light Infantry Brigades. But you yourself said that the Rajlovac Brigade ceased to exist in 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: The last piece of information I have for the Rajlovac Light Infantry Brigade was dated August 1993. Whether it continued to exist after that date, I don't know. I have no further data on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Vogosca Light Infantry Brigade was renamed 3rd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: That is correct. My data showed that the name changed sometime between October 1993 and March 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in the sketch, or the chart that we all have in front of us, both these brigades are included. Both the Vogosca and the 3rd Sarajevo Light Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: That is correct. Because the chart covers a period of time, it shows the passage of one unit to another in the same way that it shows two corps commanders in the corps headquarters when, of course, there was only ever one corps commander at any one time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My next question is this: Two brigades, the Vogosca and the 3rd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade, never existed at the same time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: Given that one was renamed to the other, I agree that they did not exist contemporaneously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you mean contemporaneously or simultaneously?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, simultaneously would be more correct. They did not exist at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since you were focussed in your study only on the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, your findings cannot be applied to any other corps of the Army of Republika Srpska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: It's -- the study of one military structure can assist in understanding other military structures, but you could not say that any other corps had the same structure as the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps except that it is based on the structure from original JNA principles. That might be the only similarity.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it true that, for example, the auxiliary organs and the number of artillery pieces is such information that cannot apply to other corps?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: The distribution of heavy weapons, such as artillery, amongst the different corps, I imagine, varied widely. I don't think you could extrapolate the weapons that were available in the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and say that, therefore, those weapons could be found elsewhere. That would not be a logical conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise if I stop. It does not mean that I'm not satisfied with your answer. It only means that I'm waiting for the interpretation to be completed. Can we agree that in addition to the fact that you did not study other VRS corps, that you also did not study any of the corps in the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I did look in detail at the -- at the 1st Corps of the ABiH at one time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say "corps," in plural, of ABH, were you referring to all the corps or only the Sarajevo-based 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the question [sic] of the witness was that he studied in detail the 1st Corps of the ABiH at one time. Of course, that does not necessarily exclude for the possibility that he also studied others, but I would have expected the witness to tell us. Could we mainly focus on what -- on -- the report of witness, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was my mistake, Your Honour. I didn't see the corner of the screen and I couldn't see "1st" because it was at the beginning of the row.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since you were studying the 1st Corps of the ABH, did you manage to discover what was the strength of the 1st Corps of the ABH? Can you tell us this today as you're sitting here?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: That is such a test of my memory that I would fail that test. I really don't remember the details of the 1st Corps of the ABiH. I produced a small chart, not in such detail as the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, based almost entirely on records that were inadmissible for court purposes, such as data from Jane's Intelligence Review and that sort of thing, so it's really a very vague indication to me of the nature of the 1st Corps. So I would be guessing now, which is of no value to the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I told you that there were about 35.000 armed members of the 1st of ABH, would that refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: No. If I were able to remember, then I would remember. But then suggesting numbers to me, I can't help you with it. I really can't. It -- if you were to ask me how many were the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, I would refer to my chart to get the correct figure, and I would look up the number from the chart. I don't remember all the detailed numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Of course. [Interpretation] Well, you have asked the next question yourself. What was the strength of the 1st -- of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: On -- on the 9th of June - I think it says - 1993, I have established a strength of 23.000 in total, including 120 active-service personnel, by which I think I understand those to be JNA -- former JNA officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since we have a smaller figure, when you made your calculation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. One second. No consultations during court time. This is the last warning, Mr. Mladic. You can write a note. You can consult with counsel during the breaks. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'll have to start my questions from the beginning. When you were calculating this figure, for example, did you take into account the Vogosca Light Infantry Brigade and the 3rd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade and their manpower? Because we can find both of them in the chart that we are looking at.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: I personally didn't calculate the figures. The number of figures would have been taken from a document. It's not simply a question of counting up how many troops there are in each of the battalions and adding them together. I don't have data on each of the battalions and each of the companies and each of the brigades. I have very partial information. Therefore, to use this chart to calculate the numbers of those present on a particular day in the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps would be misleading and not helpful. The figure I chose has come from a particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document, is it on the list that was tendered to be admitted into evidence along with your testimony? And can you tell us the source of that document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: Each of the items on the chart is listed in an alphabetical and alphanumerical list and that then supplies the source of the data for that information. And I don't have the document in front of me, but I have a reference to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the reference, please.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: I -- I hope I'm correct. I believe it to be Y000-2235 [Realtime translation read in error "22325"] is the first number. This, I believe with the prefix, would be a document that was submitted by the Galic Defence, as far as I understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's the way I understand it, too. But kindly make an effort with regard to the number, because it seems to me that there's one digit too many. I think that instead of five there should be four digits.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: Oh, I see. It's come up incorrectly. 2235. Y000-2235. And document 10 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: If it assists, that's 65 ter 12075 on our exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I cannot find this number 12075 on our list.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: It's not on -- I meant to say our 65 ter exhibit list. It's in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. It's not on the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: No, it is not on the list for --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thanks for your help. Just one moment, Your Honours. We'll probably come back to that document, but for now we have to continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Philipps, in the corps itself, there are units that are directly subordinated to the corps command, and you gave evidence to that effect. Those were units like artillery, anti-aircraft defence, logistical units, medical units, reconnaissance units, and engineers' units. In the chart that you have drawn up, are these units subordinated to the corps command or to the Corps Staff?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: The best way to understand it is that they are subordinated to the corps commander, but he exercises his control over those units through the Corps Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is a broader concept, command or staff? What denotes what?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand the question, but I'll try and explain the difference between the command and the staff. The commander gives direct orders to units that are subordinated to him. He would come up with a -- with a -- an approximation, a plan, if you like, of what activity he would like to take place, but the staff are those people that put that plan into a concrete form that can then be given to those subordinates. So although the staff write the orders, they would then be given to the corps commander for his approval before going to the troops under his command. So the staff are simply a means of facilitating the passage of orders and instructions to the troops under command and receiving data back from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what is it that the commander does when something needs to be ordered?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: The commander is the decision-maker. He -- if he decides that an attack should take place, if he decides that the units need to defend in a certain way, he makes a decision. He will then give that decision to the staff who will calculate the necessary activities; that is, how long it might take, how many troops should be involved, the nature of and quantity of ammunition. And they do what is called staff work; that is, calculate how that might work and then put that into an order that can be given to the troops. The commander really is only there to make the decision on what should be done and the staff assist him in how it should be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does the commander first make a decision or does he first present his idea or concept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: Really, the planning of an operation consists of, first of all, deciding what aim needs to be achieved. And then only the staff themselves can calculate whether that activity or action is possible. The commander makes the decision of what the aim is. It may be that the staff turn around and say, We don't have the ammunition, we don't have the artillery, we don't have the troops to fulfil that aim. So sometimes the decision of the commander is changed because of the information he receives from the staff. It's a planning meeting, if you like, a staff meeting where people coming together and discuss the capabilities of the organisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see whether I understand the answer. Are you referring to a decision-making process in which the commander has the last say, is that in short what you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your testimonies you mentioned the chief of operations. In the VRS or, rather, the SRK, the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, what is that? Chief of operations.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: The -- the chief of operations falls within the staff, and he is in charge of the planning of how operations might take place. So he falls under the command, if you like, of the staff officer who is the Chief of Staff. He's one of the planning officers for operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to put the Defence case to you and you're going to tell me whether you agree. The chief of operations is A NATO term. There was no such person in the Army of Republika Srpska. Would you agree with me or would you stand by what you had claimed; namely, that within the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, there was a chief of operations?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: I'm just referring to my alphanumeric list to look up the individual Cedo Sladoje, who is in an organisation relating to operations and training with the B/C/S abbreviation OONP. If I'm able to look at that document we could see what it says, and then we would know whether the NATO term "chief of operations" is a NATO term or whether it's used by the SRK in a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your diagram that shows the period between 1992 and 1994, Cedo Sladoje was shown as the Chief of Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. But also he was shown at another date as being part of operations and training. It -- it may be the same person. The reason there's a number after his name is it's possible that there are two people called Cedo Sladoje. I have no way of showing they are one and the same person. The document --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you're willing to take my word for it, although I am not in a position to testify, in the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps there was only one person by the name of Cedo Sladoje. So let us work on that basis.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: That would be fine, a good conclusion. I have him as being the Chief of Staff starting from August 1994, but during the period November 1992 to November 1993, in the rank of colonel, I have documents that relate to him being part of operations and training.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see that in the upper left-hand corner of your chart, in the box entitled: "Staff," or "Stab"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And I can -- have I -- if -- if it would help with an ERN, an old type of Evidence Reference Number, from documents provided by the Galic Defence, I have a combat report from a particular date that places him in that position in -- in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So with regard to this particular person or any other person who was in that position, did you consider that person to be chief of operations?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: I would have to refer to the document to see what precise title is given to the individual. Is -- is the -- is the B/C/S OONP? Does that mean operations and training? My language is not up to that understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be best that we look at the document so that we can see what name is used there for Mr. Cedo Sladoje? Could any of the parties assist in getting the right document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The witness knows.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can give the ERN if that helps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If the -- if the ERN is sufficient, then -- and otherwise if the Prosecution would have a 65 ter number, that's --

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: If you're just referring to the first ERN listed for Sladoje, Cedo, number 2, that is the same document we referred to earlier with the respect to the strength of the SRK, and that is 65 ter number 12075.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that is a document dated the 9th of June, 1993, origin, SRK command, regular combat report, with the situation at 1700 hours to the Republika Srpska army Main Staff. That's -- seems to be --

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: That seems to be the same document, Your Honour. And I identified this person that we've been speaking of, Cedo Sladoje, on page 8 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: -- in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]... see what page 8 tells us. It says: "We urgently need people for the OONP operations and training organ of the SRK, which has only 1 of 12 AVL ... NOONP, chief of the operations and training organ Colonel Cedo Sladoje." That's what the document tells us and that's the language used here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The translation is correct. So it -- what our point is -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... we now have the document before us. Please put whatever questions you'd like to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, is this the document on the basis of which you concluded that within the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps there's a chief of operations? Is that what this document says?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: I understood to mean that Colonel Cedo Sladoje was the chief of the operations and training from -- from that paragraph. I think this is also a document that has the strength of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This is the document in which the number of 23.000 appears.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will have to go back to my question; namely, whether it was on the basis of this document that you concluded that within the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps there's a chief of operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Harbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the witness has repeatedly said that he has identified this individual as the chief of operations and training. The Defence continues to refer to the chief of operations as if it is a different thing. If that is, in fact, the Defence's case, I suggest that the -- I would ask that the Defence put that to the witness. Otherwise, I think this matter has been clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to think the same way, that the matter is clarified. But I think it's clearly stated in this document as well. It's organ and in VRS --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- the organ could be one person. And that's exactly what's mentioned here and it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, whether it's more or less, it seems to say that it -- that Mr. Sladoje is the chief of the operations and training organ. Apparently there is an organ of which he is chief, and that's what the document tells us. If you have any further --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I do have another follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Philipps, according to NATO standards, what is a chief of operations?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: It's fair to say that I retired from the British Army in 2006. The chief of operations in -- from the NATO point of view is -- is -- how can I describe him? NATO has a different set of staff divisions to the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: So the staff -- staff divisions are the organisation at headquarters in the British Army is different to that of the SRK, is different to that of the former JNA, and is different to that of the Russian army. So the chief of operations would be the person responsible for putting together the planning for a particular operation, and an operation might be a movement from one place to another or it might be an attack or it might be a method of defence. And the chief of operations would work in conjunction with all the other staff officers, divided slightly differently to the -- where the corps staff is in the SRK, but the outcome would be very similar. Perhaps you might say that the Chief of Staff in the SRK is more the role of the chief of operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for this clarification. Now that we're on the subject, I'd like to ask you whether it is correct that the Main Staff, as a strategic formation, did not have artillery weapons and did not have immediate command over any part of the artillery units.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: Really, that does not form part of my report. I haven't written a chart about what the Main Staff controlled, so I have no supporting documentation showing precisely what the Main Staff commanded, the corps that it commanded, or whether it had artillery units or other units at its disposal. My simple answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question. We are have looked at this document dated the 9th of June in relation to the position of Cedo Sladoje. Now, I see in your list that there are other documents as well. There's one mentioned that's the 9th of June; but also in relation to the dates, you say it's 15th of November 1992, up to November 1993, which suggests that you have documents -- more documents from November 1992 up to November 1993. Perhaps we could, sooner or later, clarify whether that sheds any additional light on whether there was a chief of operations and training or whether there was an organ of such kind. Because you make a point out of that, Mr. Lukic. Therefore, let's inspect -- let's orient ourselves to all the sources which are apparently used here. Not necessarily to be done immediately but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think I need sometime and go through the documents that we saw today after today's working day [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Could I also invite, Ms. Harbour, that you look for other sources given for this same person in that position.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: I'll do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us briefly what makes up the command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: I would refer to my chart, first of all, 1994 -- 1992 to 1994, and it shows various staff divisions, each headed up by a staff officer. So there was part of the staff that consisted of operations and training, signals and communication, engineering staff, reinforcement and personnel, armoured operations, and artillery staff. And that would be, if you like, one staff division, one staff organisation. And then I would point to the -- a staff organisation relating to the morale of the corps. Really, that's the morale and legal and religious affairs officer. And then intelligence and security. And then logistics. And those would be the four main parts of the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The staff, as such, is it part of the corps command?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: It's part of the corps -- I see what you mean. It's part of the corps headquarters. Part of how the corps is run, but they're not directly in the chain of command. I think we've already discussed that the commander himself is the person in charge and those are merely individuals who facilitate his ability to be in charge of the organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we're going to talk about brigades a bit, actually, the brigades that were part of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. The 1st Sarajevo Mechanised Brigade. Is it correct that it actually had the composition of a battalion; and do you know how many people there were in this brigade? Do you have that particular figure?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: My chart shows that the -- the 1st Sarajevo Mechanised Brigade that you've mentioned consisted of a series of battalions, as well as supporting artillery and -- and supporting light anti-aircraft weapons, as well as logistics and a military police company. So several battalions with supporting troops. I don't -- I can't see a figure for numbers, but we do have data on some of the approximate numbers for one of the battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what that number is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: The figure for one of the infantry battalions, which was formerly the 3rd Battalion of the 1st Romanija Infantry Brigade, it was given - if my eyesight doesn't deceive me - of, I could say, 800 to 1.000. I'd have to look that up because I - like many of you - I can't quite read it. And that is a large battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Also, as you've mentioned yourself just now, there's the 1st Romanija Infantry Brigade. You don't know what its strength was - right? - because the information we have says that it was actually much smaller than what a brigade should be. That it was actually a battalion-strength level.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: I would refer to the alphanumerical list for the 1st Romanija Infantry Brigade which will provide the document where I obtained the figures showing the strength of the 1st Romanija Infantry Brigade on particular dates. I can -- I can provide the ERN if people are then able to cross-reference that to other data.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please give us that ERN number.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: I have the -- the strength numbers here of 2.824, dated the 16th of September, 1992. So then it would be a question of finding the document that is dated 16th of September, 1992, which would be ERN Y000-6240, which is a report by Colonel Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Meanwhile, I can clarify what you said. You might not be sure about reading on the chart. By enlarging it, the strength was 800 to 1.000.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And yes, there on the screen is a document that I used when compiling the report as written by Pukovnik, Dragomir Milosevic giving the strength of the brigade of 2.824, including 131 officers, 165 non-commissioned officers, and 2.528 private soldiers, which is much larger than a battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This brigade? It was singled out of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and it was attached to the Drina Corps when it was establishment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: I have no information saying that the Romanija Infantry Brigade was part of the Drina Corps. I have it as part of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. When was it resubordinated to the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] I mean -- it's my mistake, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Obviously it is time for a break, Your Honour. I have to organise my papers too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I would -- I would gladly accommodate you, Mr. Lukic. Could the witness first be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break, and we'll resume at 25 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I might use the time and draw the attention the parties to the following. On the 1st of November of this year, the Prosecution filed a bar table motion regarding eight documents which were discussed in the expert report of Dorothea Hanson and relevant to matters dealt with during the cross-examination of this witness. On 2nd November 2012, the Defence responded that it did not oppose admission of the documents and the Chamber admits the documents into evidence. And I'll read the numbers and invite Madam Registrar to assign numbers to these documents. 65 ter numbers being: 05980, 08028, 16029, 02625, 03687, 11311, 03080, and the last one, 07213.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you're ready, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Philipps, I apologise. I gave you the wrong reference number and thank you for correcting me. In your chart, on the right-hand side, I think you can see that there is mention in the second line of -- actually, under the big box where the staff is, we have the Vogosca Operations and Tactical Group and then there are three boxes on the left. In the second box there is the 2nd Motorised Brigade; however, as you can see, the abbreviation is 2 RMTBR, which actually stands for the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade. Is that correct? And that unit was also attached to the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can tell that is the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade attached to the Drina Corps on the 20th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The commander of this Motorised Brigade is Milorad Krstic, as stated here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you please assist us in finding exactly what you dealt with over the last two minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's the -- you see the big box?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Underneath the big box there are sec -- next row, yeah, the exact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Oh, there they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I found it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Philipps, Milorad Krstic is stated here as the brigade commander and, indeed, the document that you studied was a dispatch that contains the name of Milorad Krstic. However, I'm going to show you and put it to you and then you can say whether you agree or disagree. I think this is Radoslav Krstic, son of Milorad, and he was the commander of this brigade and later joined the Drina Corps and became its commander. Do you allow for this possibility? Did you find any such reference in any other document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: I would refer to you evidence reference number Y000-0657 for the original document where I obtained the information relating to Milorad Krstic in that position. And that may shed light on why I thought he was the commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a 65 ter number known for that document so that we can check?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we stipulate that it's mentioned in that document. I checked the document. But still it's not correct data. So I'm just asking if this gentleman saw something else in some other documents so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You would say this is what the document --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you have reasons to believe that it is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless, madam -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Yes. The 65 ter number is 12046, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Philipps, we did agree that the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade was separated from the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and was, in fact, attached to the Drina Corps at the time, actually, when Drina Corps was established and it became its integral part. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: Yes. My documents show that it occurred on the 20th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next box that we see here on the right, next to the 2nd Romanija Motorised Brigade, is the 1st Gradiska Light Infantry Brigade. The data that we have say that, indeed, there was such a brigade in the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps but for one month only. After that period expired it returned to Gradiska, which is the front line close to Croatia. Would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: As far as I can see from my records that I state that the 1st Gradiska Light Infantry Brigade was temporarily attached during Operation Lukovac 93 from the 1st Krajina Corps. I have no data about where it went after being temporarily attached.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me go briefly back to the 3rd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade. It's in the next line. And there is a solid line connecting it with the staff above. Is it true that the forming of the 3rd Sarajevo Light Brigade involved the brigades that were also listed in this chart, such as the Kosevo, Rajlovac, and Vogosca Brigades?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: The chart does state that the 3rd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade was formed from the Vogosca Light Infantry Brigade. And then shows the various constituents of it after that time, and it was renamed from the Vogosca to the 3rd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade at some time between October 1993 and March 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, the Vogosca Brigade is actually on the left of the box where we see the -- 3rd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade. Is it true that the Rajlovac Light Infantry Brigade also became part of the 3rd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: I have no data showing that to be the case. But if you had information showing that to be the case, then that would be a useful addition to the chart.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you have any information that the brigade shown to the right of the 3rd Sarajevo Light Brigade is the Kosevo Light Infantry Brigade, also became part of the 3rd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: Again, referring to my chart, I have no data that shows that to the case. But if we look at my later chart dated 1994 to 1995, we can see that the -- those brigades that you have mentioned no longer appear on the order of battle, and therefore they have either been renamed or resubordinated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said yourself that the structure of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps varied over a certain period of time and we can agree on that. But can you tell us the average number of the brigades that made up the SRK. So I'm looking for an average number. Was that 4, 5, 7, or 10? Do you have any idea about that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: An average over which period of time? An average based on each month, an average based on each day, or an average based on each year? If it had five for a month and then later it had seven, I don't understand how you could come up with an average number. On a particular day it had a certain number of brigades and on another day it had another number of brigades, so you could work out precisely how many brigades there were on a day-to-day basis. This -- these charts aim to show the approximate number of brigades and how each brigade may have turned into another brigade at a different time. So if we look at a chart for a particular year or a particular period of time, we can see that, for example, the Vogosca Light Infantry Brigade turns into the 3rd Sarajevo Light Infantry Brigade, but their both shown on the same chart. Not that they both existed at the same time. But it shows the progression in the same way it shows the change of leadership. We could have a chart for every month or every day that would show a different number. The number of troops rarely changed. It was just the organisation of the brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just now you said that the number of troops did not change but earlier you said that at certain points enormous losses were incurred which affected the number of troops. Later on we're going to look at the documents supporting this assertion. But if we take the year 1993, for example, do you know how many brigades were within the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps in July or any other month?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: We could take it brigade by brigade, if that would assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please give it some thought because obviously we're not going to finish today and can you give us an answer tomorrow. In the meantime, I would like to move on. Thank you. I'd like to ask you something about the security department. This section of the staff, what was their scope of responsibility? Or was that section part of the command?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: As far as I understood from the documents relating to the formation of the SRK based on -- based on the 4th JNA Corps, the security is part of the staff rather than part of the actual command. But I have very little data on the security section itself. The reason I have very little data, I think there's only one document that relates to that organisation. By its very nature, they were not -- they did not produce a great deal of documentation that we have discovered.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that all combat intelligence had to pass through this section, regardless of whether they were provided by the subordinate units, troops, or some other sources, including, inter alia, the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: Essentially I cannot answer that question. I don't know the answer to that question. I would expect that that would be the one central place where intelligence would have to pass through. That would certainly be the case with the British Army. But I have no data about the functioning of that part of the staff of the SRK, except documents that explain how the 4th JNA Corps were to function.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said today that there were battalions in the SRK that numbered only 60-odd people; is that correct? Do you know how many such battalions were in the SRK with so few people?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: No, I don't know how many had so few without researching the document in detail. Many of the brigades are shown with an approximation of the number of battalions based on the documents we've located. If we didn't locate a document pertaining to a battalion, then that battalion is not shown on the chart. It doesn't mean the battalion didn't exist. It simply means that we haven't found a document pertaining to that battalion. Most of the data did not provide the strength of battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The battalions are composed of companies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you come across information that some battalions are -- in the SRK were made up of only two companies?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: It's quite possible that the battalions were made up of a different number of companies based on their strength or their location. So some we have documents that show they had six companies and others had fewer companies. Six is an unusual number of companies for a battalion to have. Equally, two or one is an unusual number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you also found information that there were companies in the SRK that number no more than a dozen troops?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: I don't recall finding any data of that type, but it -- I would not be surprised to find companies at the strength of very few numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us go briefly now to the Vogosca Operations and Tactical Group. It's depicted in the chart under the big box that represents the staff. You spoke about this formation today as well. What is an operations group in the VRS, or, rather, in the SRK? What are its main characteristics?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: I'm by no means an expert on the use or formation of operational groups. But it appears that operational groups were formed for specific purposes, for limited periods of time, and could be formed perhaps for one operation and then disbanded and then reformed again at a later date for a different type of operation, but might consist of a different number of brigades or additional brigades depending on the situation for which they were formed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I found this already on page 29 of today's transcript which explains --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have follow-up question. I just had to remind the witness about this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So is this an operations group or a tactical group? Is that one and the same thing, the -- an operations group and a tactical group?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: In my opinion, no, they're probably not exactly the same thing. A tactical group, I suspect, is formed for a specific reason and is likely to be smaller; and an operations group will be formed for a specific operation, a larger event than a tactical group.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So during the period that you explored, and when you called this an operations and tactical group, does that mean that only one of them existed at the time or did both of them exist?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: I would have to refer to the individual documents that support the unit that's called Vogosca Operational/Tactical Group. It's worth remembering that this -- that box really only represents a headquarters. It has no troops as such. The troops are entirely made up of the brigades that become part of that group. Putting two or three brigades together with a headquarters makes an operational group. The operational group headquarters would simply have a small staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During the Galic trial --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we can call up 1D419 for that purpose. We need page 2. The trial date is the 16th [sic] of June, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Lines 9 through 13 you were asked about the Vogosca Operational/Tactical Group, and then you said: "[In English] Tell us directly. It is possible, of course, that they are two separate organisations: One, a Vogosca Operational Group; the other one a Vogosca Tactical Group." Since you said today that there is a document on the basis of which you have drawn a conclusion, are you quite clear today whether these are two or one and the same organisational group?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: Certainly at a point in time the Vogosca Operational Group existed, and at a certain point in time a Vogosca Tactical Group existed. I'd have to search the documents to see whether they both existed at the same time. I think it would be surprising if they both existed at the same time. Perhaps one existed for a period and then became a tactical group as it got smaller. But that's me surmising which is of little value to the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us agree, if possible, that you take a look at that and we shall revisit this issue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, when you read from the Galic transcript, I think the -- the vital part was missing, so could I invite you to do that again, because it now -- our transcript starts with "two separate organisations: One a Vogosca Operational Group; the other one a Vogosca Tactical Group." Could you read the whole sentence you just read again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "It is possible, of course, that they are two separate organisations: One, a Vogosca Operational Group; the other one, a Vogosca Tactical Group."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That it's just a mere possibility was not included in your quote. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This formation was definitely disbanded at certain point after it had been formed. You found out that that happened on the 15th of September, 1992. Actually, rather than me citing your findings, can you please tell me what kind of information did you discover with relation to the formation of this unit?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: It was formed at various times and various dates, and therefore one must assume that it was disbanded in between times. I refer specifically to ERN Y000-3262, which is an order by Colonel Dragan Marcetic reforming the VRS Vogosca Tactical Group on the 19th of June, 1993. So there's a series of documents listed in my alphanumeric index that relate to the formation and disbandment of the Vogosca Operational Group and the Vogosca Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, you referred to a date when it was reformed. On your chart we see it's the 19th of July, 1993, whereas you just said --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, I see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- reforming it on the 19th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I see that. The document I have in front of me has it in brackets the date 1906 -- 19-06, 1993, whereas the chart says July. So it would be worth me referring to the document to confirm the date, if that's required, whether it's June or July 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HARBOUR
utterances.text: Just to provide the 65 ter number, it's 3806.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When this organisation was established at different points in time, you don't know whether the aim of the organisation was the same every time; right? For one operation it could have been on one side of the front line, and some other time it could have had to do with a different operation.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: I suspect it was formed for different operations, but I can't see it changing from one side of Sarajevo to the other, simply because of the name of the Operational Group. It's based in and around Vogosca; hence, the name. I'd have thought if an Operational Group were to be formed elsewhere then it would have a different name. So this group was formed and reformed and disbanded at various times using the brigades in that area, such as the Ilidza Brigade, the Ilijas Brigade, the Rajlovac Brigade, and the Vogosca Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You don't have any information, or perhaps you do, whether all of these four brigades in their entirety were always part of this group. Do you know which parts; if so, can you give us some more information about that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS
utterances.text: I refer to the Evidence Reference Number I gave where a 65 ter number of 3806 was provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have a look at 1D419, page 3, yet again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you can deal with that in two minutes, it's okay as far as I'm concerned. If not, then we better adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It'd be better to continue tomorrow, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Philipps, we will adjourn for the day, and I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone or communicate in any other way with whomever about your testimony, whether testimony given today or whether testimony still to be given. If that's clear to you, we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30. Could you please follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day and we resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 8th of November, at 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom, III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 8th day of November, 2012, at 9.30 a.m.
